problem: Unity wanted new revenue from its game engine beyond seat-based subscriptions.
title: Unity introduces a per-install Runtime Fee, then cancels it
context: Unity announced a fee charged per game install for developers above revenue thresholds.
decision_made: Charge a Runtime Fee per install.
action_taken: Changed the policy after developer backlash in Sept 2023, then cancelled the fee in Sept 2024 and returned to seat-based pricing with higher Pro and Enterprise prices.
observed_outcome: Strong developer backlash; the CEO resigned in 2023; the fee was cancelled effective 12 Sept 2024.
lessons: Retroactive pricing changes for existing customers can erode trust faster than they raise revenue.
limitations: The cause of the CEO's departure and the revenue effects were not established by the sources used.

claims.claim_text: Unity introduced a Runtime Fee charged per install.
Unity cancelled the Runtime Fee for games customers and reverted to seat-based subscriptions.
